Three names. Kael had expected one, if the day went badly — maybe two.
Not three, and not in the same hand, dated the same week, tucked behind
the Registry's official trial results where no apprentice was ever
supposed to look.

Kael set the page down before their fingers could crease it.

Whoever had written this list knew exactly which climbers had failed
their trials and exactly which of those failures had never been recorded
anywhere else — climbers the Registry's public ledger simply didn't
mention, as if they had never tested at all.

Merin's name was not on the list. Kael made themselves check twice before
believing it.

But someone else's was, and that someone had eaten dinner with Kael not
four days ago, and Kael had no idea — none — what that meant, or what they
were supposed to do with knowing it, or whether the person who'd hidden
this page here had meant for it to be found by exactly this pair of hands.
